pages.title: Equivariant Symbol Calculus and Analytic Index Foundations

items.title: Finite-chart symbol calculus and equivariant Fredholm realizations

references.title: Atiyah and Singer, The index of elliptic operators I, sections 5–6

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, $E,F$ smooth finite-rank complex bundles, and fix a smooth positive density and Hermitian metrics. Write $\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$. In a chart a symbol of integer order $m$ is a smooth matrix $p(x,\xi)$ satisfying, on each compact coordinate subset,

$$|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta p(x,\xi)|\le C_{\alpha\beta}\langle\xi\rangle^{m-|\beta|}.$$

A classical symbol also has homogeneous terms $p_{m-j}(x,\xi)$, smooth for $\xi\ne0$, such that subtracting the first $N$ terms, multiplied by a cutoff zero near $\xi=0$ and one for large $\xi$, gives a symbol of order $m-N$. Quantization means

$$\operatorname{Op}(p)u(x)=(2\pi)^{-n}\int e^{ix\cdot\xi}p(x,\xi)\widehat u(\xi)\,d\xi,\qquad\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}u(x)\,dx,$$

localized by smooth cutoffs in source and target. Define $\Psi^m(X;E,F)$ to be operators given by finite sums of these local classical quantizations and operators with smooth kernels. Define integer Sobolev spaces by finite-chart Fourier norms $\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$, using distributions for negative $s$; different finite-chart choices give equivalent norms.

This class is independent of charts and frames. Its leading symbol is a well-defined smooth homogeneous bundle map $\sigma_m(P):\pi^*E\to\pi^*F$ on $T^*X\setminus0$. Every such map is realized. Composition and formal adjoint have leading symbols $\sigma(PQ)=\sigma(P)\sigma(Q)$ and $\sigma(P^*)=\sigma(P)^*$; zero leading symbol lowers the order by one. Every $P\in\Psi^m$ extends boundedly $H^s(E)\to H^{s-m}(F)$, continuously in the symbol seminorms. Negative-order operators are compact on $L^2$. An invertible leading symbol gives a two-sided parametrix in $\Psi^{-m}$ modulo smooth kernels, Fredholm realizations at every integer $s$, and distributional elliptic regularity: $Pu\in C^\infty$ implies $u\in C^\infty$.

There is a positive invertible elliptic order-one operator $\Lambda_E$ on each bundle, with scalar leading symbol $\ell(x,\xi)>0$ independent of the bundle. Its integer powers identify $H^s(E)$ with $L^2(E)$. In these equivalent norms the operator-norm closure of $\Psi^m:H^s(E)\to H^{s-m}(F)$ has a continuous surjective normalized symbol map to $C(S^*X;\operatorname{Hom}(\pi^*E,\pi^*F))$, with kernel exactly the compact operators; normalization divides the homogeneous symbol by $\ell^m$. Here $S^*X$ is any metric unit sphere bundle, with the normalization restricted to it.

Let $\overline\Psi^m$ denote the closure in all the seminorms $\|P\|_{H^s\to H^{s-m}}$, $s\in\mathbb Z$. Its leading homogeneous symbol is continuous, and invertibility gives Fredholmness at every level and smooth kernels and adjoint kernels. The kernels are independent of $s$, and smooth data in the range have smooth preimages. Smooth symbol paths admit norm-continuous quantizations; a path continuous in the classical symbol seminorms is continuous at every indicated operator norm.

If a compact Lie group $G$ acts smoothly on all the data, its section action is $(U_gu)(x)=\rho_g(g^{-1}x)u(g^{-1}x)$. Invariant density and metrics can be chosen. Conjugation $P\mapsto U_gPU_g^{-1}$ is continuous in the classical symbol seminorms and in the displayed closures. Haar averaging commutes with the symbol map and preserves these classes, orders and smooth kernels. All assertions therefore apply to $G$-invariant operators, including $G=T\times O(k)$.

items.title: Controlled equivariant symbol realization, homotopy and excision

references.title: Atiyah and Singer, The index of elliptic operators I, sections 2 and 6–8

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and $X$ a compact smooth $G$-manifold without boundary. A compact-support symbol triple on $T^*X$ consists of finite-rank continuous complex $G$-vector bundles $A,B$ and a continuous equivariant bundle map $b:A\to B$ which is an isomorphism off a compact subset. Triples are compared by equivariant bundle isomorphisms, block sum, continuous homotopies with a common compact support, and addition or removal of elementary triples whose map is everywhere invertible. These conventions concern actual bundle maps and their deformations; no previously defined equivariant $K$-group is assumed.

Every such triple has an index $a_G(A,B,b)\in R(G)$, where $R(G)$ is the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional continuous complex $G$-representations. It is realized as $[\ker P]-[\ker P^*]$ by a $G$-invariant elliptic order-zero operator on smooth bundles over $X$. Its symbol is obtained by smoothing the triple, identifying its bundles with pullbacks from the zero section by radial transport, and replacing the invertible exterior symbol by a homogeneous symbol. The index is independent of these operations, respects all the comparisons above and is additive under block sum. For a homogeneous elliptic symbol of any integer order, it equals the Fredholm index of every invariant classical or simultaneous-Sobolev-closure realization with that symbol.

The construction is natural under equivariant diffeomorphisms and restriction along homomorphisms between compact Lie groups. Tensoring all data by a finite-dimensional representation tensors the index by that representation. On a point it is the difference of the two fiber representations. For a $G$-invariant finite first-order elliptic complex on $X$, with the positive-frequency symbol and the section action $U_gu(x)=\rho_g(g^{-1}x)u(g^{-1}x)$, its symbol index is $\sum_j(-1)^j[H^j]$; its cohomology is finite dimensional and has unique harmonic representatives. This includes the de Rham complex.

Here is the controlled noncompact form. Let $U$ have an open equivariant embedding into a compact closed smooth $G$-manifold. For a compact-support triple on $T^*U$, its index can be computed after replacing it, through the same comparisons on a neighborhood of its support, by smooth base-bundle data $E,F$ and a homogeneous degree-zero symbol $c:\pi^*E\to\pi^*F$ for which $E=F=U\times V$ and $c=I_V$ outside a compact invariant subset of $U$, with $V$ a finite-dimensional representation. There is an elliptic invariant realization equal to the exterior bundle isomorphism off one compact invariant $L\subset U$, in both the source and target kernel variables; explicitly it has the form $P=\eta_2P_0\eta_1+h(1-\eta_1)$ with nested compactly supported cutoffs and exterior isomorphism $h$. Extending the bundles and this operator to any compact equivariant ambient manifold by the exterior trivializations gives the same virtual kernel representation. Thus the index is independent of that ambient embedding and satisfies excision for open equivariant inclusions whenever such compact ambients are supplied. No compactification of an arbitrary $G$-manifold is asserted.

items.title: Positive-order associated-bundle product and its equivariant index

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I, §9, pp. 526–529
Searchable compilation of Atiyah–Singer papers I–III; paper I, §§5–6 and 9

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T$ and $H$ be compact Lie groups, with no connectedness or commutativity requirement on $H$. Let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal right $H$-bundle over a compact smooth manifold without boundary. Let $T$ act smoothly on $P$ on the left, commuting with $H$, and let $F$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary with commuting smooth left actions of $H$ and $T$. Put $Y=P\times_H F$, where $(p h,f)$ is identified with $(p,hf)$, and let $p_Y:Y\to X$ be its projection. The action of $t\in T$ on $Y$ is $[p,f]\mapsto[tp,tf]$.

Let $E^0,E^1\to X$ be smooth Hermitian $T$-bundles and $G^0,G^1\to F$ smooth Hermitian $H\times T$-bundles. Choose invariant densities and metrics. Let $A:C^\infty(X,E^0)\to C^\infty(X,E^1)$ and $B:C^\infty(F,G^0)\to C^\infty(F,G^1)$ be respectively $T$- and $H\times T$-equivariant elliptic operators of order one, allowing the following precise closure: an operator is in the order-one Sobolev closure if classical order-one operators converge to it in every norm $H^s\to H^{s-1}$, $s\in\mathbb Z$, with the compatible continuous degree-one principal symbol provided by the compact symbol calculus. Extend their degree-one symbols $a(x,\xi)$ and $b(f,\eta)$ by zero at the zero covector. They are invertible for nonzero covectors.

Write $\mathcal G^j=P\times_H G^j\to Y$ and $\mathcal E^{ij}=p_Y^*E^i\otimes\mathcal G^j$. There are compatible $T$-equivariant horizontal lifts

$$A_j:C^\infty(Y,\mathcal E^{0j})\longrightarrow C^\infty(Y,\mathcal E^{1j}),\qquad j=0,1,$$

in the order-one Sobolev closure. Let $B_i:\mathcal E^{i0}\to\mathcal E^{i1}$ denote the fiberwise operator induced by $B$. On smooth sections these lifts obey all four exact identities

$$B_1A_0=A_1B_0,\qquad B_0^*A_1^*=A_0^*B_1^*,\qquad B_1^*A_1=A_0B_0^*,\qquad B_0A_0^*=A_1^*B_1.$$

The adjoints are with respect to the invariant product density on $Y$ obtained from the base density and the $H$-invariant fiber density. Define

$$D=\begin{pmatrix}A_0&-B_1^*\\ B_0&A_1^*\end{pmatrix}:\mathcal E^{00}\oplus\mathcal E^{11}\longrightarrow\mathcal E^{10}\oplus\mathcal E^{01}.$$

Then $D:H^1\to L^2$ is Fredholm, both its kernel and its adjoint kernel are finite-dimensional smooth $T$-representations, and its principal symbol represents the graded product of $a$ and $b$. Explicitly, a connection splitting of a covector on $Y$ into horizontal $\xi$ and vertical $\eta$ gives the product symbol

$$d_{\mathrm{prod}}(y;\xi,\eta)=\begin{pmatrix}a(p_Yy,\xi)\otimes I&-I\otimes b(f,\eta)^*\\ I\otimes b(f,\eta)&a(p_Yy,\xi)^*\otimes I\end{pmatrix}.$$

This matrix is interpreted using an associated-bundle trivialization; its homotopy class is independent of the connection. The actual glued lift symbol need only be homotopic through invertible joint symbols to this matrix.

Let $K=\ker B$ and $L=\ker B^*$, with their finite-dimensional $H\times T$ actions, and put $K_P=P\times_H K$, $L_P=P\times_H L$. The restricted lifts give elliptic operators $C_K:E^0\otimes K_P\to E^1\otimes K_P$ and $C_L$ with $K$ replaced by $L$, whose symbols are $a\otimes I$. For $\operatorname{Ind}_T Q=[\ker Q]-[\ker Q^*]\in R(T)$, where $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional continuous complex $T$-representations, one has

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T D=\operatorname{Ind}_T C_K-\operatorname{Ind}_T C_L.$$

Thus the analytic symbol index of the associated product is the base symbol index twisted by the associated virtual vertical index $K_P-L_P$. For a product bundle with independent commuting group actions this specializes to multiplication of representation-valued indices. The same external-product identity holds for compactly supported elliptic symbol data on invariant open manifolds when their indices are defined by the controlled compactification and excision construction.

items.title: Orthogonal-equivariant compact normalization of the doubled-real Bott symbol

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I, Annals of Mathematics 87 (1968), 484–530
references.locator: Lemma 3.2, pp. 499–500; proposition 4.4 and lemma 4.7, pp. 505–508; §8, pp. 524–526.

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb R^n$ with its Euclidean inner product and standard action of $O(n)$, including $n=0$. Identify $T^*V$ with $V\oplus V$ by the metric and put $z=x+i\xi\in V_{\mathbb C}$. On the constant graded bundle $\Lambda^\bullet V_{\mathbb C}$ define $k(z)=\varepsilon_z+\varepsilon_z^*$, where $\varepsilon_z$ is exterior multiplication and the star is the Hermitian adjoint. The even-to-odd part is invertible off the origin since $k(z)^2=(|x|^2+|\xi|^2)I$. Let $b_V$ be its compact-support equivariant symbol class.

Here a compact-support symbol class means a stabilized pair of finite-rank equivariant complex bundles and an equivariant bundle map invertible outside an invariant compact subset, modulo compact-support homotopy and addition of everywhere invertible maps. Its compact-support analytic index is obtained by a controlled order-zero realization after extension to the compact sphere $S(V\oplus\mathbb R)=V\cup\{\infty\}$. For this class the result is

$$a_{O(n)}(b_V)=1\in R(O(n)),$$

the trivial one-dimensional representation. More generally, restriction along any compact Lie group homomorphism $G\to O(n)$ and tensoring by a finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation $E$ give $a_G(b_V\otimes E)=[E]$. This normalization therefore includes nontrivial orthogonal actions on the real normal fiber in an associated-bundle construction.

The complex orientation is fixed by $z=x+i\xi$: in one plane the even-to-odd map is $z$, the root Bott generator clutched by $z$. The cotangent form is $\theta=\sum_j\xi_jdx_j$, so $d\theta=\sum_jd\xi_j\wedge dx_j$. On $T^*V$ the complex-coordinate orientation and the orientation $(d\theta)^n/n!$ differ by $(-1)^n$. No orientation reversal or complex conjugation is inserted into $b_V$.

items.title: Fourier–Hardy index and the sign of the cotangent plane symbol

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I, Annals of Mathematics 87 (1968), 484–530
references.locator: §8, printed pp. 525–526, the Hardy projection and rectangle clutching computation.

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $S^1=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, with coordinate $x$ and density $dx/(2\pi)$. Let a compact Lie group $G$ act trivially on $S^1$ and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional unitary complex $G$-representation. On $L^2(S^1;V)$ let $P_+$ be the orthogonal projection onto the closed span of $e^{inx}v$ with $n\ge0$. The bounded operator

$$A=e^{ix}P_++(1-P_+)$$

is an equivariant order-zero elliptic pseudodifferential operator. Its leading symbol on the two components of the cotangent sphere is $e^{ix}I_V$ at $\xi>0$ and $I_V$ at $\xi<0$. Its kernel is zero, its cokernel is the constant copy of $V$, and $\operatorname{Ind}_G(A)=-[V]$.

Write $b\in K_c^0(T^*\mathbb R)$ for the relative complex line symbol $x+i\xi$, invertible outside the origin. The group $K_c^0$ here means stabilized finite complex bundle symbols invertible outside a compact set, modulo compact-support homotopies and addition of everywhere invertible symbols. The plane generator uses the complex coordinate $x+i\xi$ and therefore is the root Bott class clutched by $z$. After a degree-one symbol homotopy the symbol of $A$ is supported in a coordinate interval, and its class there is $-b\otimes V$. Thus the compact-support analytic index of $b$ is $1$.

For clarity about orientation, the tautological cotangent form is $\theta=\xi\,dx$ and $d\theta=d\xi\wedge dx$. The positively oriented boundary for the complex plane $x+i\xi$ traverses the top of a rectangle from right to left. The Hardy symbol winds $-1$ on that boundary. Reversing to the $d\theta$ orientation reverses both boundary windings; it does not change the class identity $[\sigma(A)]=-b\otimes V$.

items.title: Equivariant compact-support symbol classes and the normal Koszul class

references.title: Graeme Segal, Equivariant K-theory, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 34 (1968), 129–151
M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I, Annals of Mathematics 87 (1968), 484–530

items.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, $r\ge0$, act continuously on a locally compact Hausdorff space $X$. All vector bundles below have finite complex rank and continuous $T$-linearizations. A **compact-support symbol triple** is $(A,B,s)$, where $A,B\to X$ are such bundles and $s:A\to B$ is an equivariant bundle map that is an isomorphism outside an invariant compact subset of $X$. Isomorphic triples have intertwining bundle isomorphisms. A homotopy of triples is such a triple over $X\times[0,1]$, with trivial action on $[0,1]$, whose noninvertibility set lies in $C\times[0,1]$ for some invariant compact $C\subset X$. A triple is elementary when $s$ is an isomorphism on all of $X$.

Define $K^0_{T,c}(X)$ to be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these triples, subject to the relations that direct sum is addition, elementary triples are zero, and the two endpoints of a homotopy represent the same class. Define $K^1_{T,c}(X)=K^0_{T,c}(X\times\mathbb R)$, with trivial action on $\mathbb R$. Here $c$ means compact support. For any base $Y$, write $K_T^0(Y)$ for the Grothendieck ring of equivariant vector bundles on $Y$. On compact $Y$, the natural map $[W]\mapsto[W,0,0]$ identifies this with the triple presentation: $s$ can be homotoped to zero, and $(W,W,I)$ can be homotoped to $(W,W,0)$, giving precisely the direct-sum and inverse relations. On a point the bundle Grothendieck ring is the representation ring $R(T)$, whose multiplication is tensor product and whose element $[W]$ has character $g\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(g|W)$. Tensoring both bundles and the map of a triple with the pullback of a representation defines the $R(T)$-module structure on $K^q_{T,c}(X)$, $q=0,1$.

For a smooth compact $T$-manifold $M$, give $T^*M$ the cotangent action: $t$ sends $(x,\xi)$ to $(t\cdot x,\xi\circ(dt_x)^{-1})$. Let $A:C^\infty(M,E^+)\to C^\infty(M,E^-)$ be a first-order differential operator between smooth finite-rank equivariant complex bundles. The smooth bundle actions have fiber maps $\rho_t^\pm(x):E_x^\pm\to E_{t\cdot x}^\pm$, satisfying $\rho_e^\pm(x)=I$ and $\rho_{st}^\pm(x)=\rho_s^\pm(t\cdot x)\rho_t^\pm(x)$; on sections set $(U_t^\pm u)(x)=\rho_t^\pm(t^{-1}\cdot x)u(t^{-1}\cdot x)$. Require $AU_t^+=U_t^-A$. If $A=\sum_{|\alpha|\le1}a_\alpha(x)\partial_x^\alpha$ in local coordinates and frames, put $a(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=1}a_\alpha(x)(i\xi)^\alpha$. The operator is elliptic when $a(x,\xi):E_x^+\to E_x^-$ is invertible for every real $\xi\ne0$. Its **compact symbol class** is

$$[\sigma(A)]=[\pi^*E^+,\pi^*E^-,a]\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*M),$$

where $\pi:T^*M\to M$ is the projection. The zero section is compact; the differential intertwining identity makes its symbol equivariant. If an $L^2$ realization $A:H^1(M,E^+)\to L^2(M,E^-)$ is Fredholm and the metrics are invariant, its **analytic equivariant index** is $[\ker A]-[\ker A^*]\in R(T)$, where $A^*$ denotes its Hilbert-space adjoint. These finite-dimensional kernels carry the induced $T$-representations. Fredholmness is a hypothesis here, not a consequence stipulated by the definition.

For a Hermitian equivariant complex vector bundle $W\to Y$, write $\pi_W:W\to Y$ for its projection. On $\pi_W^*\Lambda^\bullet W$ define $\varepsilon_w$ to be exterior multiplication by the tautological vector $w\in W_y$, and let $\varepsilon_w^*$ be its Hermitian adjoint. The **Koszul symbol** is $\kappa_W=(\varepsilon_w+\varepsilon_w^*)|_{\mathrm{ev}}$ from even to odd exterior powers. It satisfies $(\varepsilon_w+\varepsilon_w^*)^2=|w|^2I$, so it is invertible off the zero section. On a complex line with coordinate $z$, its even-to-odd map is multiplication by $z$; this fixes its Bott sign. If $Y$ is noncompact, this is a class with support proper over $Y$, not a compact-support class on $W$ by itself. Its zero-section restriction is the virtual bundle

$$\lambda_{-1}(W)=\sum_{j=0}^{\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}W}(-1)^j[\Lambda^jW]\in K_T^0(Y).$$

For a real equivariant normal bundle $\nu\to F$ supplied with an invariant inner product, identify $\nu^*$ with $\nu$. The doubled normal bundle $\nu\oplus\nu^*$ has complex structure $J(v,w)=(-w,v)$, so is identified with $\nu_{\mathbb C}=\nu\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$. The real inner product extends complex-bilinearly to a nondegenerate equivariant pairing on $\nu_{\mathbb C}$, hence gives a complex-linear equivariant isomorphism $\nu_{\mathbb C}\cong\nu_{\mathbb C}^*$. Its Koszul zero-section class $\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C})$ can therefore also be written $\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*)$. This identification is asserted for a complexified real bundle, not for an arbitrary Hermitian complex bundle. For $g\in T$ fixing the base point $x\in F$, the character of this virtual fiber is

$$\operatorname{tr}\!\left(g\middle|\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C,x}^*)\right)=\det_{\mathbb C}(I-g|_{\nu_{\mathbb C,x}^*}).$$

This follows by expanding the exterior-power trace as the product of $1-\lambda$ over the complex eigenvalues $\lambda$. For orthogonal $g$, this determinant equals the real determinant $\det_{\mathbb R}(I-g|_{\nu_x})$ and is positive when $g$ has no fixed normal vector: nonreal eigenvalues occur in conjugate pairs, and a real eigenvalue different from $1$ is $-1$.

items.title: Fixed-inclusion localization for equivariant compact symbol classes

references.title: Graeme Segal, Equivariant K-theory, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 34 (1968), 129–151
references.locator: §§1–3, especially propositions 2.6, 2.9 and 3.5; §4, proposition 4.1, printed pp. 144–145.

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary. Fix $g\in T$, put $F=M^g$, and choose a $T$-invariant metric. Write $\nu=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F$, $p:T^*F\to F$, and $X=T^*M$. The inclusion $j:T^*F\to X$ extends a covector by zero on $\nu$. It is a proper embedding and $X^g=j(T^*F)$. Its real normal bundle is $p^*(\nu\oplus\nu^*)$, with complex structure $J(v,\eta)=(-\eta^\sharp,v^\flat)$, hence is the complex bundle $W=p^*\nu_{\mathbb C}$. Put

$$e=\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*)\in K_T^0(F),\qquad S_g=\{s\in R(T):s(g)\ne0\}.$$

Here $s(g)$ is the character value of the virtual representation $s$; localization means tensoring an $R(T)$-module with $S_g^{-1}R(T)$. In both degrees $q=0,1$, restriction is an isomorphism

$$j^*:S_g^{-1}K^q_{T,c}(T^*M)\xrightarrow{\cong}S_g^{-1}K^q_{T,c}(T^*F).$$

The Koszul symbol on $W$, followed by extension from a tubular neighborhood, defines a homomorphism $j_!:K^q_{T,c}(T^*F)\to K^q_{T,c}(T^*M)$. Its self-intersection formula and localized reconstruction formula are

$$j^*j_!(b)=p^*e\,b,\qquad a=j_!\bigl((p^*e)^{-1}j^*a\bigr).$$

The inverse in the second formula exists as a module endomorphism after $S_g$-localization. These identities hold for every compact-support symbol class, including the class of every equivariant elliptic operator, with no Dirac-type or isolated-fixed-point restriction.

Since $g$ fixes $F$ pointwise, a bundle $E$ on $F$ has $g$-eigenbundles $E_\zeta$. The $g$-character homomorphism is $\operatorname{tr}_g[E]=\sum_\zeta\zeta[E_\zeta]\in K^0(F)\otimes\mathbb C$, extended to fractions by division by $s(g)$. For the denominator it gives

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(e)=\prod_\zeta\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\operatorname{rank}E_\zeta}(-\zeta)^k[\Lambda^kE_\zeta]\right),\qquad E=\nu_{\mathbb C}^*.$$

Every eigenvalue $\zeta$ here differs from $1$. The rank of this ordinary $K$-class at $x\in F$ is $\det_{\mathbb C}(I-g|_{\nu_{\mathbb C,x}^*})=\det_{\mathbb R}(I-g|_{\nu_x})\ne0$. At an isolated fixed point this is exactly the real determinant. On a positive-dimensional component the whole virtual bundle, rather than just its rank, is required in the reconstruction formula.

items.title: Trace-weighted compact symbol character and the cotangent pushforward

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I
Peter B. Gilkey, Invariance Theory, the Heat Equation, and the Atiyah-Singer Index Theorem, first edition, §4.4
James L. Heitsch, The Lefschetz Principle, Fixed Point Theory, and Index Theory, Theorem 2.1

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, possibly disconnected and nonorientable. Let $h$ be a unitary bundle automorphism covering the identity of $F$, obtained from the action of a fixed element of a compact torus, and acting on all symbol bundles compatibly with their maps. Put $n=\dim F$ componentwise. For a compact-support symbol class $a$ on $T^*F$, its trace-weighted compact-support Chern character is

$$\operatorname{ch}_{h,c}(a)=\sum_{\lambda}\lambda\,\operatorname{ch}_c(a_\lambda)\in H_c^{\mathrm{even}}(T^*F;\mathbb C),$$

where $a_\lambda$ is its symbol class on the $\lambda$-eigenbundles of $h$. The sum is finite on each compact disk-bundle representative; it is extended linearly to virtual classes. Here $\operatorname{ch}_c$ is the relative topological Chern character, not the Chern character of the alternating bundle restricted to the zero section.

Fix the following cotangent orientation and Bott normalization. If $\theta=\sum_j\xi_jdx_j$ is the tautological one-form, orient $T^*F$ by $(d\theta)^n/n!$, namely by $d\xi_1\wedge dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\xi_n\wedge dx_n$. The plane Bott class is the even-to-odd symbol $z:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ on the plane $z=x+i\xi$, with its relative-triple convention corresponding to $[\gamma]-1$ for the tautological Hopf line. Write $p_{F,!}:K_c^0(T^*F)\to\mathbb Z$ for the embedding construction: use this Bott Thom class on the doubled real normal bundle of an embedding $F\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$, extend by zero into $T^*\mathbb R^N$, and invert the same plane Bott external product on $T^*\mathbb R^N$. Its trace-weighted extension is $p_{F,!,h}(a)=\sum_\lambda\lambda p_{F,!}(a_\lambda)$. Then

$$p_{F,!,h}(a)=\int_{T^*F}\operatorname{ch}_{h,c}(a)\,\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(TF\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C).$$

For a degree-$2n$ compact-support cohomology class, the integral means its pairing with the relative fundamental class $[D_R(T^*F),S_R(T^*F)]$, using a radius $R$ containing its support in the disk interior, excision and the indicated orientation of the total space. Only the degree-$2n$ part is paired, and components are summed. This definition uses an orientation of the cotangent total space and requires no orientation of $F$.

The Todd class of a complex bundle with formal Chern roots $x_j$ means $\prod_j x_j/(1-e^{-x_j})$, expanded only through the dimension of the base. The integer construction is independent of the chosen embedding and tubular data.

In particular, let $M$ be a compact smooth torus manifold, $g$ a torus element, $F$ a component of $M^g$, $\nu$ its real normal bundle, and $i:T^*F\hookrightarrow T^*M$ the inclusion using an invariant metric. Put $e_g=\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*)$ and let $\sigma\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*M)$ be any compact elliptic symbol class. The character of $e_g$ at $g$ is nonzero, and the trace-weighted Chern character extends to localization at virtual representations whose character at $g$ is nonzero. Whenever the representation-localized K-group supplies a class $b$ with $e_g b=i^*\sigma$ (in particular, the quotient $b=i^*\sigma/e_g$ furnished by K-localization), one has

$$p_{F,!,g}(b)=\int_{T^*F}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}(i^*\sigma)}{\pi^*\operatorname{ch}_g(\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*))}\,\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(TF_{\mathbb C}).$$

This is the characteristic-class comparison for a fixed component. It applies to the compact symbol of a general first-order elliptic complex after forming its even-to-odd elliptic symbol. It does not assert localization of equivariant K-theory or equality of analytic and topological indices; those are separate prerequisites for identifying the sum of these expressions with an analytic character. With the other common cotangent symplectic convention $-d\theta$, both displayed integrals acquire the factor $(-1)^n$.

items.title: Analytic symbol index, normal embedding compatibility and ordinary pushforward

references.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I, §§4 and 7–9

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on compact smooth manifolds without boundary. The compact-symbol triple group has a homomorphism

$$a_{T,M}:K^0_{T,c}(T^*M)\longrightarrow R(T)$$

which sends the symbol of an equivariant elliptic operator to its analytic kernel-minus-adjoint-kernel index, and sends the folded symbol of a first-order elliptic complex to its alternating cohomology representation. It is $R(T)$-linear and respects equivariant diffeomorphisms and restriction of the acting group.

Let $f:Y\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth equivariant embedding of compact manifolds, with real invariant metric normal bundle $N$. Extend a covector on $Y$ by zero on $N$ to obtain $j:T^*Y\hookrightarrow T^*M$. Its normal bundle is $\pi_Y^*(N\oplus N^*)$, with complex structure $J(v,\eta)=(-\eta^\sharp,v^\flat)$. Define $j_!$ by pulling a symbol to this complex normal, taking its graded product with exterior multiplication by $v+i\eta^\sharp$ plus its adjoint on $\Lambda^\bullet N_{\mathbb C}$, and extending from a tubular neighborhood. Then, for every $c\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*Y)$,

$$a_{T,M}(j_!c)=a_{T,Y}(c).$$

This includes arbitrary symbol classes and real normal bundles, without a Dirac-type or fixed-point-dimension restriction.

For the trivial group, embed $Y$ into $\mathbb R^N$ and form the same doubled-normal extension $j_!c\in K_c^0(T^*\mathbb R^N)$. This group is generated by the plane Bott product with plane map $z=x+i\xi$. Its integer coefficient is denoted $p_{Y,!}(c)$. One has

$$a_{\{1\},Y}(c)=p_{Y,!}(c).$$

In particular that integer is independent of the embedding. If $g\in T$ fixes $Y$ pointwise, its action splits a symbol into finitely many $g$-eigenbundle classes $c_\lambda$ on each compact disk representative, and

$$\chi_{a_{T,Y}(c)}(g)=\sum_\lambda\lambda\,p_{Y,!}(c_\lambda).$$

Every identity extends to localization at the virtual representations whose character at $g$ is nonzero, by division by that character. No assertion of an index distribution for transversally elliptic symbols is made.

items.title: A compact symbol at a point retains the full torus character
items.statement: Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, let $M=\{p\}$, and put $\mathbb C_k=\mathbb C$ with $[s]\in T$ acting by $e^{2\pi i k s}$. Take $E^0=\mathbb C_0\oplus\mathbb C_1$, $E^1=\mathbb C_2$, with differential zero. The compact symbol triple on $T^*M=\{p\}$ is $(E^0,E^1,0)$. Its virtual bundle is $[\mathbb C_0]+[\mathbb C_1]-[\mathbb C_2]$, whose character at $g=[s]$ is $1+z-z^2$, $z=e^{2\pi i s}$. This is also the cohomological index character. The normal Koszul denominator is $1$ because the normal bundle has rank zero.

items.title: Construction and Thom Compatibility of Borel Fiber Integration

references.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
references.locator: Sections 2–3, equivariant integration and Thom pushforward conventions.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 3.3, Poincaré duality and the cup pairing.

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, let $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, and use the product right Milnor model and associated-bundle equivalence $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Let $X$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff second-countable smooth $n$-manifold without boundary, with a smooth orientation-preserving $T$-action. Put $X_T=ET\times_T X$. For $N\geq0$, put $E_N=(S^{2N+1})^r$, $B_N=(\mathbb{CP}^{N})^r$, $X_N=E_N\times_T X$, and $p_N:X_N\to B_N$. The finite sphere models embed in the chosen $ET$, inducing $j_N:B_N\to BT$ and $a_N:X_N\to X_T$. Orient $B_N$ by its product complex orientation and $X_N$ by base orientation followed by fiber orientation. Write $b_N=2Nr$.

For $a\in H^q(X_N;k)$, define $(p_N)_!a\in H^{q-n}(B_N;k)$ as the unique class satisfying, for every $b\in H^{b_N-q+n}(B_N;k)$,

$$\langle b\smile(p_N)_!a,[B_N]\rangle=\langle p_N^*b\smile a,[X_N]\rangle.$$

Groups in negative degrees are zero. For $d=q-n\geq0$ and $2N+1\geq d$, the map $j_N^*:H^d(BT;k)\to H^d(B_N;k)$ is an isomorphism, and

$$\int_X\alpha=(j_N^*)^{-1}(p_N)_!a_N^*\alpha\qquad(\alpha\in H^q(X_T;k))$$

is independent of such $N$. For $d<0$ define it to be zero. In every degree its restriction to every finite $B_N$ is $(p_N)_!a_N^*\alpha$. Thus this specifies an actual degree-$-n$ Borel fiber pushforward, including rational coefficients, without a differential-form model on the infinite-dimensional base.

It is linear over $H^*(BT;k)$ with coefficients on the left, commutes with $\mathbb Q\to\mathbb R$, and restricts at a point of $BT$ to ordinary oriented integration. For a trivial action it sends $v\otimes z$ to $v\langle z,[X]\rangle$, where the latter is zero unless $z$ has degree $n$. Product fiber integration is iterated integration in the stated orientation order. These maps extend to character-localized modules by $\int_X(\alpha/s)=(\int_X\alpha)/s$.

Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a compact closed equivariant embedded boundaryless submanifold with invariant oriented normal bundle $\nu$ and $o(TX|_Y)=o(TY)\wedge o(\nu)$. Whenever its Borel Thom class is supplied, define $i_*^T$ by multiplying the pulled-back class of $Y_T$ on the left by the normalized Thom class on the right, then applying tubular excision and the relative-to-absolute map. Then

$$\int_X i_*^T\beta=\int_Y\beta.$$
